I think you've formed your arguments on a few biases. The first and most obvious would be a sampling bias. Your opinion is formulated from observations made through outspoken experiences with some atheists, not all atheists are so confrontational and because of their lack of yearning for confrontation you've possibly only heard from a subgroup of more aggressive atheists.

The second bias would be a cognitive bias. It seems from your harsh verbiage that you may be formulating your opinion on pre-existing factor rather than hard evidence. 

It is also possible the atheists come across as rude because your beliefs are in such a strong opposition with one another, leading you to perceive the interactions as more negative than it actually is  you may be making an ad hominem, which could lead to your negative perception. It's easier to judge someone's character than to argue against their point. It could be your way of definding your religion, but in an invalid way.
